summary:
Farmboost is an agronomic decision-support platform that helps small and medium-sized farmers choose the best crop rotation for their fields using open-source satellite data from NASA and other space agencies. The farmer marks their land with a single click on the map, selects what they are currently growing, and chooses their primary goal (saving water, protecting the soil, or stabilizing the harvest). Immediately afterward, the system cross-references 20 years of daily climate data from NASA POWER, SMAP soil moisture data, SRTM/DEM elevation data, physical soil properties (ISRIC Soil Grids), and Sentinel-2 imagery to simulate the daily water balance (FAO-56/33) for four rotation scenarios and generate a PDF report for the agronomist. The project makes precision agriculture more accessible, reducing losses due to drought or excessive rainfall and protecting soil health without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)
details:
The producer accesses the high-resolution map, locates their property via city search or GPS, and marks the area with 1 click (or draws the exact boundary of the plot). From the georeferenced polygon, Farmboost queries scientific APIs in real time:

  • NASA POWER: 20-year daily series of temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, humidity, and wind.
  • NASA GIBS & CMR: visual layers (MODIS, VIIRS, Blue Marble) and coverage verification of SMAP L3/L4, ECOSTRESS, SRTM 30m, and GEDI L4A.
  • Complementary sources: ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (clay, sand, organic carbon, and available water capacity), Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A (STAC catalog), ECMWF ERA5, and Open-Meteo DEM (slope and erosion risk). With this data, the agronomic engine runs a daily water balance simulation (FAO-56 and FAO-33 yield response) over the past 20 years, comparing 4 strategies: current management, legume/grass cover, drought-tolerant second crop, and crop-livestock integration. The system calculates crop failure risk, median yield (P50) and dry year yield (P10), water savings (m³/ha), and assigns easy-to-understand scores. Benefits and intended impact:
  • Translates complex satellite data into accessible language for small and medium-sized farmers.
  • Helps prevent crop failures due to drought or extreme rainfall, reduces erosion, and improves soil organic matter.
  • Exports a technical PDF report with equations, sources, and data gaps for validation with an agronomist. Tools, languages, and technologies used:
  • Frontend & Geoprocessing: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, Turf.js, and Lucide Icons.
  • Export & Hosting: jsPDF (in-browser PDF report generation) and Cloudflare Workers.
  • APIs and Open Data: NASA POWER, NASA GIBS (WMTS), NASA CMR, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0, Copernicus Sentinel-2 STAC, ECMWF ERA5, Open-Meteo Elevation, and OpenStreetMap Nominatim.

Creative aspect and factors considered by the team:

Farmboost's biggest differentiator is combining scientific rigor (20 years of daily FAO-56/33 simulation and full transparency regarding what is measured vs. estimated) with an interface designed for those in the field: 1-click marking, goal shortcuts.

Translated with Gemini (free version)
